scope.note: Removes a check: any court's review of the reasonableness of decisions by the government, prime minister or ministers, including appointments and refusals to act; the text provides no alternative mechanism.

required_majority_met.note: Not coded (protocol limits this variable to enactments 2 and 3); 64 in favor for reference.

deviation_tier.support: לא ידון בעניין סבירות ההחלטה ... ולא ייתן צו בעניין כאמור
deviation_tier.note: Values engaged: rule of law (principal: judicial review of executive action), separation of powers, independent judiciary. Sharp: a categorical bar on any court hearing or ordering on reasonableness for the whole elected executive, extended expressly to appointments and non-exercise of powers. Alternative reading Limited (other grounds of review untouched).

direction.support: lo yadun: courts barred from reviewing reasonableness of government, PM and ministerial decisions
direction.note: Axis engaged: narrowing of judicial review. No identity or minority axis.

deviations: Knesset websites (fs.knesset.gov.il, main.knesset.gov.il, m.knesset.gov.il, knesset.gov.il/Odata) answered every request with 'The site is temporarily inaccessible from your location'. A text-proxy route gave the same notice and web.archive.org is not fetchable from this tool. Consequences: no gazette text for enactments 2, 6 and 8; no bills/explanatory notes for 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 (8's notes only as quoted in press); no Knesset vote or reading records for 1, 2, 3, 8, 9. Vote and reading data for those were taken from press reports, as the sheet permits; government composition from Wikipedia articles on the governments, as the sheet permits when the Knesset site is unreachable.

Knesset records used for enactment 4 are the NYU Faculty Digital Archive's copies of Divrei HaKnesset (13th Knesset sittings of 8 and 15 February and 8 and 9 March 1994), read by local text extraction. Its only 1969 sitting near enactment 2's passage (20 February 1969) is an image-only scan I could not read; no July–August 1969 sitting is held there.

Pages opened and closed without using anything, because they treat a court's handling of an enactment: palquest.org entry on Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty (opened for the 1992 tally; discusses the Supreme Court's interpretation); a 1970 ZaöRV law report 'Staatliche Wahlkampffinanzierung der Parteien in Israel' (opened for enactment 2's passage date; its introduction turns to the court's 3 July 1969 decision); Globes 24 April 2001 'ללא חופש ביטוי' (discusses a 1995 ruling). The passage date of enactment 2 is therefore left blank.

Web-search result summaries repeatedly described court rulings on enactments 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9 and litigation documents hosted by the Israel Democracy Institute; none of those pages was opened and nothing from the summaries was used. Hebrew Wikisource's pages for enactments 8 and 9 carry editorial tags naming court cases next to the gazette references; I used only the statutory text and disregarded the tags. This is why enactment 8's immediate_effect is blank: the consolidated text shows a deferral label whose provenance (gazette or court) I cannot establish from permitted sources.

Sources outside the strict list, and why: (a) the gazette page for enactment 9 was read from a scan hosted by the Israel Democracy Institute (it is the Reshumot page itself, two pages, no commentary) because the Knesset copy is blocked; (b) the 1992 tally and 'December 1991' first reading for enactment 1 and the 19 July 2016 first reading for enactment 5 rest on sentences from the search engine's index of an Israel Hayom opinion piece and a Jerusalem Post report, since the pages returned 403 or headline-only on direct fetch; (c) Wikipedia's article on Rafi Peretz was consulted but the coding of his status rests on the 35th-government article and a Maariv report of the House Committee decision of 14 July 2020; (d) enactment 6's content is taken from Walla and Calcalist descriptions because no copy of the gazette text was reachable.

Could not find in any permitted source: the original 1969 text of enactment 2 (its title is known from enactment 3's text); the vote tallies, reading dates and explanatory notes of enactments 2 and 3; the exact first-reading date and any faction breakdown of the 17 March 1992 vote on enactment 1; the explanatory notes of enactments 4, 5, 6 and 9; the commencement wording of enactments 6 and 8. Cells depending on these are blank with the search described in their notes.

The vote extract for enactment 6 labels Rafi Peretz 'Yamina'; press and the government article show he had split into a separate Jewish Home faction on 14 July 2020 and was a serving minister, so I coded coalition_only Yes and recorded the discrepancy.

Tool limitation: pdftotext is not installed; PDFs were extracted with pypdf from the user's Python site-packages. OCR was unavailable for image-only scans (the 20 February 1969 sitting; the 1970 State Comptroller report).
